title: Sa Pa is planning fruit, flowers, and a reason to stay after dark
summary: On 13 October the ward held a workshop on four projects: temperate fruit, a flower landscape, a night-time economy, and digital kiosks with public Wi-Fi. They are proposals and site visits, not a new night market with posted hours.
when: Workshop on 13 October 2026. Night hours: Check on arrival.
photoAlt: A water wheel in Cat Cat village, Sa Pa
body: Sa Pa is trying to give the day a second half. On the afternoon of 13 October the ward People’s Committee held a workshop on four projects from its party resolution for 2025–2030: temperate fruit trees native to the place, a flower landscape, a night-time economy, and digital kiosks with public Wi-Fi. Lào Cai’s paper says the night-time idea is specialised streets and services that would stretch the hours a visitor can use. Cao Tấn Dương, of the State Audit Office, argued that a mountain town’s night depends less on how much concrete is poured than on who organises it and who benefits. He offered five moves: an identity for “Sa Pa night,” a time-limited pilot, local people as the main parties, one coordination desk, and a way to measure whether it works. No opening hour is in the report. Check on arrival.

The other three projects are just as unfinished, and just as specific. Nguyễn Phương Lan of Cat Cat Tourism, drawing on 15 years in the village, described a greener Sa Pa carried by residents, businesses, and visitors together, with flowers as something to come and see through the year. Lâm Văn Thuận, of a Sa Pa plum business, said a commercial stand of Sa Pa red plums could work if the volume stays limited and the quality is controlled, and he proposed visits for blossom, harvest, and processing, plus plum-blossom honey, plum wine, dried plums, and syrup. That is his proposal, not a shop list checked on a shelf. Delegates then went to see fruit at Sau Chua, a flower garden near the Fansipan cable-car station, night-time activity in the Northwest, and a pilot kiosk at the Sa Pa cultural market. The photograph is a water wheel in Cat Cat, the village named in the flower discussion.

sources.label: Báo Lào Cai, via Vietnam.vn, 14 October 2026
